from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Meet Vector Vic, a robot with a mission.', 
            'He must reach target vector B using paths V1, V2.', 
            'How many units of each path does Vic need?'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Quest of Vector Vic", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define a coordinate system inside the grid area B1 to F6
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 8, 2],
            y_range=[0, 12, 2],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B1', 'F6')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Vector Vic (robot) at origin
        vic_circle = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1)
        vic_label = Text("V", font_size=16, color=BLACK).move_to(vic_circle.get_center())
        vic_group = VGroup(vic_circle, vic_label)
        vic_group.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(vic_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight current line (using Green as the main mission color)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Define the base vectors
        v1_color = "#0000FF" # Blue
        v2_color = "#FF0000" # Red
        b_color = "#00FF00"  # Green
        
        v1_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(2, 1), buff=0, color=v1_color)
        v1_label = Text("V1", font_size=20, color=v1_color).next_to(v1_arrow.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        v2_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1, 3), buff=0, color=v2_color)
        v2_label = Text("V2", font_size=20, color=v2_color).next_to(v2_arrow.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Target vector B
        b_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(7, 11), buff=0, color=b_color)
        b_label = Text("B", font_size=24, color=b_color).next_to(b_arrow.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(v1_arrow), Write(v1_label))
        self.play(Create(v2_arrow), Write(v2_label))
        self.play(Create(b_arrow), Write(b_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight current line (Yellow for unknown variables)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Equation text at the top of the animation area
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        equation = Text("x V1 + y V2 = B", font_size=32, t2c={"x": "#FFFF00", "y": "#FFFF00"})
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'A1', 'A6')
        
        # Step-by-step path to B: 2*V1 + 3*V2
        path_v1_1 = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(2,1), buff=0, color=v1_color, stroke_width=3)
        path_v1_2 = Arrow(plane.c2p(2,1), plane.c2p(4,2), buff=0, color=v1_color, stroke_width=3)
        
        path_v2_1 = Arrow(plane.c2p(4,2), plane.c2p(5,5), buff=0, color=v2_color, stroke_width=3)
        path_v2_2 = Arrow(plane.c2p(5,5), plane.c2p(6,8), buff=0, color=v2_color, stroke_width=3)
        path_v2_3 = Arrow(plane.c2p(6,8), plane.c2p(7,11), buff=0, color=v2_color, stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show two V1s
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(v1_arrow, path_v1_1))
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(path_v1_1, path_v1_2))
        
        # Show three V2s
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(v2_arrow, path_v2_1))
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(path_v2_1, path_v2_2))
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(path_v2_2, path_v2_3))
        
        # Move Vic along the resulting path to reach B
        self.play(
            vic_group.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(7, 11)),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with provided script
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Determinant as Area", 
            [
                "The determinant represents the area of a parallelogram.", 
                "V1 and V2 form this area in our grid.", 
                "A zero area means no solution is possible."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1 in Yellow to match the parallelogram concept
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Blue vector V1 #0000FF and red vector V2 #FF0000
        # Position using grid indices: Origin at F2, V1 at E4 (2,1 offset), V2 at C3 (1,3 offset)
        v1 = Arrow(self.grid['F2'], self.grid['E4'], buff=0, color="#0000FF", stroke_width=6)
        v2 = Arrow(self.grid['F2'], self.grid['C3'], buff=0, color="#FF0000", stroke_width=6)
        
        # Labels for vectors
        v1_label = Text("V1", font_size=24, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(v1_label, 'E5') # Within 1 grid unit of end point E4
        v2_label = Text("V2", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(v2_label, 'B3') # Within 1 grid unit of end point C3

        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Change lecture line focus
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF") # Keep white or light highlight
        
        # A yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 at 0.3 opacity forms between V1 and V2
        # Sum vertex is at B5 (4.5, 1.2) = Origin (1.5, -2.8) + (3, 4)
        poly_points = [self.grid['F2'], self.grid['E4'], self.grid['B5'], self.grid['C3']]
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            *poly_points, 
            fill_color="#FFFF00", 
            fill_opacity=0.3, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        # The area of the parallelogram is labeled 'Area = 5' in yellow #FFFF00.
        area_label = Text("Area = 5", font_size=32, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(area_label, 'C4', 'D5') # Center in the parallelogram body
        
        self.play(FadeIn(parallelogram))
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        
        # The boundary vectors V1 and V2 flash white #FFFFFF simultaneously.
        self.play(
            v1.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            v2.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            run_time=0.4
        )
        self.play(
            v1.animate.set_color("#0000FF"),
            v2.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            run_time=0.4
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight zero area / no solution warning in Red
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # Text 'det(V1, V2) = 5' appears below the shape in white #FFFFFF.
        det_text = Text("det(V1, V2) = 5", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, 'F4')
        
        self.play(Write(det_text))
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "The Vector Combination Problem"
        lines = [
            "Solution x and y scale our basis vectors.",
            "We stretch V1 and V2 to reach target B.",
            "Cramer's Rule solves this using area ratios."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        V1_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        V2_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        B_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        COORD_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # Coordinate System setup
        scale_val = 0.35
        
        vector_field = VGroup()
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 9, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 13, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        vector_field.add(plane)

        # Basis vectors (using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' dependency)
        i_hat_dummy = Vector([1, 0], color=V1_COLOR)
        j_hat_dummy = Vector([0, 1], color=V2_COLOR)
        i_label = Text("i", color=V1_COLOR, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(i_hat_dummy.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_label = Text("j", color=V2_COLOR, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(j_hat_dummy.get_end(), LEFT)
        
        # Target Vectors
        v1_dummy = Vector([2, 1], color=V1_COLOR)
        v2_dummy = Vector([1, 3], color=V2_COLOR)
        v1_label = Text("V1", color=V1_COLOR, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(v1_dummy.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v2_label = Text("V2", color=V2_COLOR, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(v2_dummy.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        b_vec_dummy = Vector([7, 11], color=B_COLOR)
        b_label = Text("B", color=B_COLOR, font_size=28, slant=ITALIC).next_to(b_vec_dummy.get_end(), UP)
        
        # Solution Coordinates (Yellow)
        coords_label = Text("(2, 3)", color=COORD_COLOR, font_size=32).next_to(b_vec_dummy.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # Positioning the visualization
        self.place_in_area(vector_field, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=scale_val)
        
        # Helper to create vectors correctly scaled by the plane
        def get_v_in_plane(coords, color):
            start = plane.get_origin()
            end = plane.c2p(coords[0], coords[1])
            return Vector(end - start, color=color).shift(start)

        vi_anim = get_v_in_plane([1, 0], V1_COLOR)
        vj_anim = get_v_in_plane([0, 1], V2_COLOR)
        v1_anim = get_v_in_plane([2, 1], V1_COLOR)
        v2_anim = get_v_in_plane([1, 3], V2_COLOR)
        vb_anim = get_v_in_plane([7, 11], B_COLOR)

        # Sync labels to transformed positions
        i_l = i_label.scale(1.2).next_to(vi_anim.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_l = j_label.scale(1.2).next_to(vj_anim.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        v1_l = v1_label.scale(1.2).next_to(v1_anim.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v2_l = v2_label.scale(1.2).next_to(v2_anim.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        b_l = b_label.scale(1.2).next_to(vb_anim.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        c_l = coords_label.scale(1.2).next_to(vb_anim.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(plane, vi_anim, vj_anim, i_l, j_l)
        self.wait(1)

        matrix = [[2, 1], [1, 3]]
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            Transform(vi_anim, v1_anim),
            Transform(vj_anim, v2_anim),
            Transform(i_l, v1_l),
            Transform(j_l, v2_l),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        v1_scaled = get_v_in_plane([4, 2], V1_COLOR).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        v2_scaled = get_v_in_plane([3, 9], V2_COLOR).set_stroke(opacity=0.5).shift(v1_scaled.get_end() - plane.get_origin())
        
        self.play(Create(vb_anim), Write(b_l))
        self.play(Create(v1_scaled), Create(v2_scaled), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Write(c_l))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        parallelogram = Polygon(
            plane.get_origin(),
            v1_anim.get_end(),
            v1_anim.get_end() + (v2_anim.get_end() - plane.get_origin()),
            v2_anim.get_end(),
            fill_opacity=0.3,
            fill_color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(parallelogram))
        self.play(Indicate(parallelogram))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(parallelogram), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            'Replace the first path, V1, with target B.',
            'Form a new parallelogram with B and V2.',
            'This new area is exactly x times the original.',
            'Comparing these areas reveals our unknown value, x.',
            'Area ratios provide a geometric bridge to algebra.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Trick: Replacing a Column", lines)

        # Define Geometric Elements
        # Origin for our coordinate system on the grid
        origin_point = self.grid['E2']
        
        # Vectors relative to the chosen origin
        v1_vec = np.array([1.5, 0, 0])
        v2_vec = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        b_vec = np.array([3.0, 0, 0]) # x=2 relative to v1
        
        # Manim Objects (Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency)
        v1 = Arrow(origin_point, origin_point + v1_vec, buff=0, color="#0000FF")
        v2 = Arrow(origin_point, origin_point + v2_vec, buff=0, color="#FF0000")
        b = Arrow(origin_point, origin_point + b_vec, buff=0, color="#00FF00")
        
        v1_label = Text("V1", color="#0000FF").scale(0.6)
        v2_label = Text("V2", color="#FF0000").scale(0.6)
        b_label = Text("B", color="#00FF00").scale(0.6)
        
        # Positioning labels using grid logic
        self.place_at_grid(v1_label, 'E3')
        self.place_at_grid(v2_label, 'D1')
        self.place_at_grid(b_label, 'F4')
        
        # Parallelograms
        poly_orig = Polygon(
            origin_point, 
            origin_point + v1_vec, 
            origin_point + v1_vec + v2_vec, 
            origin_point + v2_vec, 
            fill_opacity=0.4, 
            fill_color="#FFFF00", 
            stroke_color="#FFFF00"
        )
        
        poly_new = Polygon(
            origin_point, 
            origin_point + b_vec, 
            origin_point + b_vec + v2_vec, 
            origin_point + v2_vec, 
            fill_opacity=0.4, 
            fill_color="#00FF00", 
            stroke_color="#00FF00"
        )
        
        area_label_orig = Text("Area = 5", color="#FFFF00").scale(0.6)
        area_label_new = Text("Area = 10", color="#00FF00").scale(0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(area_label_orig, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(area_label_new, 'B4')
        
        # Initial state: V1, V2 and original area
        self.add(v1, v2, v1_label, v2_label, poly_orig, area_label_orig)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(v1),
            FadeOut(v1_label),
            FadeOut(poly_orig),
            FadeOut(area_label_orig),
            FadeIn(b),
            FadeIn(b_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Create(poly_new))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Write(area_label_new))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        
        eq1 = Text("x = New Area / Original Area", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        eq2 = Text("x = 10 / 5", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        eq3 = Text("x = 2", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(eq1, 'A3')
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, 'A3')
        self.place_at_grid(eq3, 'A3')

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Script and Layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'Why does replacing the column work so perfectly?',
            'Target B consists of components xV1 and yV2.',
            'The yV2 component shears the shape, preserving area.',
            'Only the xV1 component contributes to the new area.',

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Shearing and Scaling Logic", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual Parameters
        v1_color = BLUE
        v2_color = RED
        b_color = "#00FF00"
        xv1_color = BLUE_A
        yv2_color = PINK
        para_color = YELLOW
        
        # Coordinate Space (Axes placed in specific grid area)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 3.5, 1], y_range=[-0.5, 3.5, 1],
            x_length=3.5, y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6")
        origin = axes.c2p(0, 0, 0)
        
        # Vector Data
        v1_val = np.array([1.2, 0.4, 0])
        v2_val = np.array([0.4, 1.3, 0])
        x_coeff = 1.3
        y_coeff = 0.8
        
        xv1_val = x_coeff * v1_val
        yv2_val = y_coeff * v2_val
        b_val = xv1_val + yv2_val

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # REPLACED MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        v1 = Arrow(origin, axes.c2p(*v1_val), buff=0, color=v1_color)
        v2 = Arrow(origin, axes.c2p(*v2_val), buff=0, color=v2_color)
        v1_lab = Text("V1", color=v1_color, font_size=20).next_to(v1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v2_lab = Text("V2", color=v2_color, font_size=20).next_to(v2.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), Write(v1_lab), Write(v2_lab))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        b_vec = Arrow(origin, axes.c2p(*b_val), buff=0, color=b_color)
        b_lab = Text("B", color=b_color, font_size=22).next_to(b_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        xv1_line = DashedLine(origin, axes.c2p(*xv1_val), color=xv1_color)
        xv1_lab = Text("xV1", color=xv1_color, font_size=18).next_to(xv1_line.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        yv2_line = DashedLine(axes.c2p(*xv1_val), axes.c2p(*b_val), color=yv2_color)
        yv2_lab = Text("yV2", color=yv2_color, font_size=18).next_to(yv2_line.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(b_vec), Write(b_lab))
        self.play(Create(xv1_line), Write(xv1_lab))
        self.play(Create(yv2_line), Write(yv2_lab))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Original Parallelogram (B, V2)
        p_pts = [origin, axes.c2p(*v2_val), axes.c2p(*(v2_val + b_val)), axes.c2p(*b_val)]
        para = Polygon(*p_pts, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=para_color, stroke_color=para_color, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(FadeIn(para))
        
        # Shear tracker: slide B tip back to xV1
        s_val = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        def update_para(p):
            s = s_val.get_value()
            curr_b = xv1_val + s * yv2_val
            current_pts = [origin, axes.c2p(*v2_val), axes.c2p(*(v2_val + curr_b)), axes.c2p(*curr_b)]
            p.set_points_as_corners([*current_pts, current_pts[0]])
            
        para.add_updater(update_para)
        
        # B vector tip follows the shear
        b_moving = Arrow(origin, axes.c2p(*b_val), buff=0, color=b_color)
        b_moving.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(origin, axes.c2p(*(xv1_val + s_val.get_value() * yv2_val))))
        
        # Remove old static elements
        self.remove(b_vec, b_lab, yv2_line, yv2_lab)
        self.add(b_moving)
        
        self.play(s_val.animate.set_value(0), run_time=3)
        para.clear_updaters()
        b_moving.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Height indicator relative to V2
        v2_dir = v2_val / np.linalg.norm(v2_val)
        v2_norm = np.array([-v2_dir[1], v2_dir[0], 0])
        h_mag = np.dot(xv1_val, v2_norm)
        h_pt = xv1_val - h_mag * v2_norm
        
        h_line = DashedLine(axes.c2p(*xv1_val), axes.c2p(*h_pt), color=WHITE)
        h_lab = Text("Height", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(h_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        base_brace = Brace(Line(origin, axes.c2p(*v2_val)), LEFT, color=v2_color, buff=0.1)
        base_lab = Text("Base", font_size=16, color=v2_color).next_to(base_brace, LEFT, buff=0.05)
        
        self.play(Create(base_brace), Write(base_lab))
        self.play(Create(h_line), Write(h_lab))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with provided lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'To find x, divide modified area by original area.', 
            'To find y, replace V2 with B and divide.', 
            'For Vic, x is 10 divided by 5, which is 2.', 
            'And y is 15 divided by 5, which is 3.', 
            'Vic reaches his goal with 2 V1s and 3 V2s!'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Formula and Conclusion", lecture_lines)

        # Vector Vic data
        v1_coords = np.array([1, 0.5, 0])
        v2_coords = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        x_val, y_val = 2, 3
        b_coords = x_val * v1_coords + y_val * v2_coords

        # Colors
        COLOR_X = WHITE
        COLOR_Y = "#FF0000" # Red as requested

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # x formula: x = det(B, V2) / det(V1, V2)
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' dependency error
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_X))
        x_formula = Text(
            "x = det(b, v2) / det(v1, v2)",
            color=COLOR_X
        )
        self.place_in_area(x_formula, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(x_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # y formula: y = det(V1, B) / det(V1, V2)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_Y))
        y_formula = Text(
            "y = det(v1, b) / det(v1, v2)",
            color=COLOR_Y
        )
        self.place_in_area(y_formula, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(y_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Numerical x: x = 10 / 5 = 2
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_X))
        x_calc = Text("x = 10 / 5 = 2", color=COLOR_X)
        self.place_in_area(x_calc, 'C2', 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(x_calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Numerical y: y = 15 / 5 = 3
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_Y))
        y_calc = Text("y = 15 / 5 = 3", color=COLOR_Y)
        self.place_in_area(y_calc, 'C4', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(y_calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Coordinate system and Vic's movement
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1], 
            y_range=[0, 7, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        
        # Draw vectors and point B
        v1_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*v1_coords), buff=0, color=BLUE)
        v2_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0,0), plane.c2p(*v2_coords), buff=0, color=COLOR_Y)
        b_dot = Dot(plane.c2p(*b_coords), color=YELLOW)
        b_label = Text("b", color=YELLOW).next_to(b_dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        v1_label = Text("v1", color=BLUE).next_to(v1_arrow.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        v2_label = Text("v2", color=COLOR_Y).next_to(v2_arrow.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        visual_group = VGroup(plane, v1_arrow, v2_arrow, b_dot, b_label, v1_label, v2_label)
        self.place_in_area(visual_group, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.55)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(Create(v1_arrow), Create(v2_arrow), Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(b_dot), Write(b_label))
        
        # Vic's path
        vic = Dot(plane.c2p(0,0,0), color=PINK, radius=0.1)
        vic_label = Text("Vic", font_size=16, color=PINK).next_to(vic, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        
        # Update label to follow Vic
        vic_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(vic, DOWN, buff=0.05))
        
        self.add(vic, vic_label)
        
        # Path 1: 2 * V1
        path1_end = 2 * v1_coords
        self.play(vic.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(*path1_end)), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Path 2: + 3 * V2
        self.play(vic.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(*b_coords)), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students learning Linear Algebra

sections.title: Introduction: The Quest of Vector Vic
sections.content: Introduce a character, 'Vector Vic' the robot, who needs to reach a specific target (Vector B) using only two fixed power paths (Vectors V1 and V2). The problem is framed as: How many units of V1 and V2 does Vic need? This sets up the linear system Ax = b.
sections.example: Vic stands at (0,0). V1 is a path going 2 units right, 1 unit up. V2 is 1 unit right, 3 units up. The target B is at (7, 11). How many V1s and V2s reach B?

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Determinant as Area
sections.content: Before solving the puzzle, we define the determinant. Visually demonstrate that the determinant of a 2x2 matrix is the signed area of the parallelogram formed by its column vectors. If the vectors are 'squished' together, the area is zero (no solution).
sections.example: Show a blue vector (2,1) and a red vector (1,3). Animate a yellow parallelogram forming between them. The determinant (2*3 - 1*1 = 5) represents the area of this shape.

sections.title: The Vector Combination Problem
sections.content: Show that finding the solution (x, y) means stretching V1 by 'x' and V2 by 'y' so they sum up to B. This creates a transformation where the unit square is stretched into the parallelogram we just saw. This sets the stage for Cramer's insight: area ratios.
sections.example: Animate the 'Recipe': x * [2, 1] + y * [1, 3] = [7, 11]. The grid deforms, showing how B lands somewhere in the coordinate system of V1 and V2.

sections.title: The Geometric Trick: Replacing a Column
sections.content: Explain the core of Cramer's Rule: If we replace V1 with the target vector B, the area of the new parallelogram (B and V2) is exactly 'x' times the area of the original parallelogram (V1 and V2). This is because only the component of B along V1 contributes to the change in area relative to V2.
sections.example: Visually replace the blue vector (V1) with the green vector (B). Show the original parallelogram (Area = 5) and the new one formed by B and V2 (Area = 10). The ratio 10/5 gives us x = 2.

sections.title: Shearing and Scaling Logic
sections.content: Use a 'shearing' animation to show why this works. Since B = xV1 + yV2, when we take the determinant of (B, V2), the 'yV2' part doesn't add any area because it's parallel to V2. We are left with the determinant of (xV1, V2), which is just x * det(V1, V2).
sections.example: Animate the parallelogram formed by (xV1 + yV2) and V2. Show the 'yV2' component sliding along V2 like a deck of cards (shearing), which doesn't change the area, leaving only the 'xV1' contribution.

sections.title: The Formula and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize Cramer's Rule as a ratio of areas. X is the area of the 'modified' parallelogram divided by the 'original' area. Generalize this to Y by replacing the second column. Conclude by solving Vector Vic's original problem.
sections.example: Final calculation display: x = det(B, V2) / det(V1, V2) = 10 / 5 = 2. y = det(V1, B) / det(V1, V2) = 15 / 5 = 3. Vector Vic needs 2 units of path V1 and 3 units of path V2!

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Quest of Vector Vic
lecture_lines: Meet Vector Vic, a robot on a mission.
He has two movement paths, V1 and V2.
His goal is to reach the target vector B.
How many steps of each path does he take?
We model this quest as a linear system.
animations: A white circle #FFFFFF labeled 'V' representing Vic appears at the origin.
Blue arrow V1 #0000FF and red arrow V2 #FF0000 extend from the origin.
A green arrow B #00FF00 pointing to (7, 11) appears as the target.
Two blue V1 arrows and three red V2 arrows align tip-to-tail to reach B.
White text 'x V1 + y V2 = B' appears at the top, with 'x' and 'y' in yellow #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: Start with our two direction vectors, V1 and V2.
They span a parallelogram in the coordinate plane.
This shape's area is the key to our solution.
Algebraically, we call this area the determinant.
For these vectors, the determinant equals five.
animations: Blue vector V1 #0000FF and red vector V2 #FF0000 are shown on a black background.
A yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 at 0.3 opacity forms between V1 and V2.
The area of the parallelogram is labeled 'Area = 5' in yellow #FFFF00.
The boundary vectors V1 and V2 flash white #FFFFFF simultaneously.
Text 'det(V1, V2) = 5' appears below the shape in white #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Vector Combination Problem
lecture_lines: Think of V1 and V2 as a new grid.
Target B sits at a specific spot here.
We need B's coordinates in this custom basis.
animations: The background basis vectors i and j transform into V1 #0000FF and V2 #FF0000.
Target vector B [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] #00FF00 is highlighted at its position relative to the V1-V2 basis.
Coordinates '(2, 3)' appear next to the tip of B in yellow #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: The Geometric Trick: Replacing a Column
lecture_lines: Look back at our original area of five.
Swap the first vector V1 for target vector B.
This swap creates a brand new green parallelogram.
The new area measures exactly ten units.
The ratio of areas gives us the solution x.
animations: Show the original yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 with area labeled '5'.
The blue vector V1 is removed and replaced by the green vector B #00FF00.
A new green parallelogram #00FF00 forms using B and V2 (red).
The new area is calculated and labeled 'Area = 10' in green #00FF00.
The expression 'x = 10 / 5' appears in white #FFFFFF, then simplifies to 'x = 2'.

storyboard.title: Shearing and Scaling Logic
lecture_lines: Vector B is made of V1 and V2 parts.
The V2 component shears the shape without changing area.
Only the V1 component determines the area's scale.
animations: Vector B #00FF00 is shown as the vector sum of x*V1 and y*V2 components.
The y*V2 component of the parallelogram [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] (B, V2) slides (shears) along the direction of V2.
A visual indicator shows that the height and base relative to V2 remain unchanged, preserving area.

storyboard.title: The Formula and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Cramer's Rule uses these area ratios for any variable.
Solving for y, we find a result of three.
Vic follows the paths and reaches his target!
animations: A general mathematical formula for x and y using determinants appears in white #FFFFFF.
Calculation 'y = 15 / 5 = 3' is displayed in red #FF0000 to match the V2 substitution.

Vic [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vic.svg] moves along the calculated path (2*V1 then 3*V2) to reach the target [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] B.
